name: Explicit Mertens bounds for $\sum_{p\le x}\log p/p$: Decomp1528a
description:
For a real cutoff $x\ge1$, consider the weighted prime sum $\sum_{p\le x}\log p/p$, where $p$ ranges over primes and $\log$ is the natural logarithm. Mertens' first theorem says that this sum differs from $\log x$ by a bounded amount. This mission asks for the explicit bound $\left|\sum_{p\le x}\log p/p-\log x\right|\le2$ over the entire stated range.

The open statements also concern the logarithm of a factorial, finite sums of $\log p/[p(p-1)]$, and the von Mangoldt function $\Lambda$, which equals $\log p$ at positive prime powers and zero elsewhere. Chebyshev's functions $\theta$ and $\psi$ record the corresponding accumulated logarithmic weights. These objects provide explicit control of prime sums used in analytic number theory and sieve estimates. Exact constants and endpoint ranges matter when such estimates feed into quantitative results about almost primes, integers with few prime factors.

The source context is P. J. Campbell, [A Sharper Explicit Result for the Sum of Two Almost Primes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09488v1), Section 4. The lab identifies the classical background as Rosser and Schoenfeld, *Approximate formulas for some functions of prime numbers*, Illinois Journal of Mathematics 6, 1962, especially p. 70, with factorial identities also attributed to Ingham and Montgomery and Vaughan. These are lab formulations of classical material, rather than a claim that every displayed leaf is printed verbatim in Campbell.

The statements come from an AI-run Lean lab. Drafts undergo human audit before submission to the public platform; this draft is prepared for that audit. The mission contains eleven open leaves and one assembly goal, using only Mathlib objects. No new mathematical result is claimed, and Goldbach's conjecture remains open.

items.theorem_title: Legendre upper bound for the logarithm of a factorial
items.formal_statement:
namespace LL_Decomp1528a
theorem log_factorial_le_sum (n : ℕ) :
    log (n.factorial : ℝ) ≤
      (n : ℝ) * ∑ p ∈ Nat.primesLE n, log p / p +
        (n : ℝ) * ∑ p ∈ Nat.primesLE n, log p / ((p : ℝ) * ((p : ℝ) - 1)) := by sorry
end LL_Decomp1528a
items.natural_language_statement: For every natural number $n$, $\log(n!)\le n\sum_{p\le n}\frac{\log p}{p}+n\sum_{p\le n}\frac{\log p}{p(p-1)}$, where both sums run over primes.
items.preamble:
import Mathlib

open Real Finset Chebyshev

items.theorem_title: Legendre lower bound using the Chebyshev function
items.formal_statement:
namespace LL_Decomp1528a
theorem sum_sub_theta_le_log_factorial (n : ℕ) :
    (n : ℝ) * ∑ p ∈ Nat.primesLE n, log p / p - θ n ≤ log (n.factorial : ℝ) := by sorry
end LL_Decomp1528a
items.natural_language_statement: For every natural number $n$, $n\sum_{p\le n}\frac{\log p}{p}-\theta(n)\le\log(n!)$, where $\theta(n)=\sum_{p\le n}\log p$ and the sums run over primes.

items.theorem_title: Explicit bound for the prime sum through $1000$
items.formal_statement:
namespace LL_Decomp1528a
theorem sum_log_div_pp1_head :
    ∑ p ∈ Nat.primesLE 1000, log p / ((p : ℝ) * ((p : ℝ) - 1)) ≤ 0.7545 := by sorry
end LL_Decomp1528a
items.natural_language_statement: The finite sum over primes satisfies $\sum_{p\le1000}\frac{\log p}{p(p-1)}\le0.7545$.

items.theorem_title: Uniform bound for the integer tail beyond $1000$
items.formal_statement:
namespace LL_Decomp1528a
theorem sum_log_div_pp1_tail (n : ℕ) :
    ∑ m ∈ Ioc 1000 n, log m / ((m : ℝ) * ((m : ℝ) - 1)) ≤ 0.009 := by sorry
end LL_Decomp1528a
items.natural_language_statement: For every natural number $n$, $\sum_{1000<m\le n}\frac{\log m}{m(m-1)}\le0.009$, with the sum over integers and with an empty sum when $n\le1000$.

items.theorem_title: Prime sum bounded by a fixed head and an integer tail
items.formal_statement:
namespace LL_Decomp1528a
theorem sum_log_div_pp1_split (n : ℕ) :
    ∑ p ∈ Nat.primesLE n, log p / ((p : ℝ) * ((p : ℝ) - 1)) ≤
      ∑ p ∈ Nat.primesLE 1000, log p / ((p : ℝ) * ((p : ℝ) - 1)) +
        ∑ m ∈ Ioc 1000 n, log m / ((m : ℝ) * ((m : ℝ) - 1)) := by sorry
end LL_Decomp1528a
items.natural_language_statement: For every natural number $n$, $\sum_{p\le n}\frac{\log p}{p(p-1)}\le\sum_{p\le1000}\frac{\log p}{p(p-1)}+\sum_{1000<m\le n}\frac{\log m}{m(m-1)}$, where $p$ runs over primes and $m$ over integers.

theorem mertens1_small {x : ℝ} (hx : 1 ≤ x) (hx5 : x < 5) :

items.theorem_title: Chebyshev identity for the logarithm of a factorial
items.formal_statement:
namespace LL_Decomp1528a
theorem log_factorial_eq_vonMangoldt (n : ℕ) :
    log (n.factorial : ℝ) =
      ∑ m ∈ Icc 1 n, ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt m * ((n / m : ℕ) : ℝ) := by sorry
end LL_Decomp1528a
items.natural_language_statement: For every natural number $n$, $\log(n!)=\sum_{m=1}^{n}\Lambda(m)\lfloor n/m\rfloor$, where $\Lambda(m)=\log p$ if $m$ is a positive power of a prime $p$, and $\Lambda(m)=0$ otherwise.

items.theorem_title: Upper bound for the weighted von Mangoldt sum
items.formal_statement:
namespace LL_Decomp1528a
theorem vonMangoldt_sum_le (n : ℕ) :
    (n : ℝ) * ∑ m ∈ Icc 1 n, ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt m / m ≤
      log (n.factorial : ℝ) + ψ n := by sorry
end LL_Decomp1528a
items.natural_language_statement: For every natural number $n$, $n\sum_{m=1}^{n}\frac{\Lambda(m)}{m}\le\log(n!)+\psi(n)$, where $\Lambda$ is the von Mangoldt function and $\psi(n)=\sum_{m=1}^{n}\Lambda(m)$. The statement includes $n=0$.
